sources.note: Lexical isogloss bundles across the Bomboma, Nieuw-Antwerpen and Budzala territories; no prosody at all.

sources.citation: Grégoire, Claire. 2003. The Bantu languages of the forest. In D. Nurse & G. Philippson (eds), The Bantu Languages, ch. 19, pp. 349-370. London: Routledge. Section 2.3 Tonality, p. 357.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Second-hand: Ngiri languages between the Ngiri and the Ubangi (Zamba, Lobala, Bomboma, Lingonda, Ebuku) 'have a very complicated tonality'; 'In Bomboma, nominal forms show tonal modifications that depend on their function and place in the clause.' Cites Toronzoni 1985 in its bibliography. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1990. Parlers riverains de l'entre Ubangi-Zaïre: éléments de structure grammaticale. (Études Aequatoria 8.) Bamanya: Centre Aequatoria. Chapter 'Le parler des Ebuku', pp. 13-32.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1 Phonologie (pp. 14-16) covers vowels, consonants, vowel harmony, coalescence, elision, gliding; 'Tonologie' (pp. 16-18) gives noun tone correspondences with Lingala-type tonology, high-toned prefixes in prepositional groups, final-syllable H in questions, tonal harmony from the final. No word 'accent'/'intensité'/'pénultième' anywhere in the chapter (the one 'quantité à la pénultième' remark at p. 69 is in the Libobi sketch, not Ebuku/Bomboma).

sources.citation: Motingea Mangulu, André. 1989. Sur les parlers riverains de la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 281-283; and Explorations linguistiques dans la Ngiri. Annales Aequatoria 10: 353-357.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classification and fieldwork diary (Ebuku = Lingonda notes collected at Mankanza, March 1988); Zamba singled out for a wholly different tonology (citing De Boeck 1951). Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. De tonologie der naamwoorden te Ebuku. Kongo-Overzee 16(5): 281-291 (with 'Slotbeschouwingen' on all six Ngiri varieties).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Noun tonology only (initial tone types, tone melodies before/after other words, high initial tone after another word, final tones lengthened before pause). Informant from Ebuku, 'sector and territory Bomboma'. No statement on stress/klemtoon. The only 'klemtoon' hit in the volume (16(1): 65) is Burssens's review of an Indonesian textbook, irrelevant.

sources.citation: De Boeck, L. B. 1950. Eigenaardige toonstructuur van enkele Bantoetalen in het Noord-Westen van Belgisch-Kongo. Kongo-Overzee 16(1): 36-52 (+ continuations on Iniele/Bokonzi 16(2-3), Maleke-Moleke/Moliba 16(4)).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction to the series: the 'inverted' (Tshiluba-like) noun tone melodies are located 'vooral in het gewest Bomboma'. Tone only; nothing on stress.
